cars.generation: Original Sonett II body family, selected V4 production coupe
cars.specification_market: Original SAAB 1968 Sonett V4 USA brochure, ten-page scan. Contact sheet and PDF8/10 individually read, including USA distributor footer. Both native SAE and DIN ratings are preserved with their distinct engine speeds, not converted. Selected 1498-cc V4, not the two-stroke II, later Sonett III or 1.7-litre engine. cars.summary: The Sonett V4 gave Saab a distinctly unconventional sports car, combining front-wheel drive, a freewheel transmission and a fibreglass body over a steel chassis. Its compact V4-powered aerodynamic coupe body and standard roll bars express an individual approach to the small sports-car formula.

cars.generation: René Bonnet / Matra original mid-engine Djet road family
cars.variant: Djet 5 — Lane Motor Museum 1108-cc road reference
cars.specification_market: Lane Motor Museum’s own Djet 5 collection page supplies this 1108-cc OHV, water-cooled, mid-engine, rear-drive four-speed reference. Its current heading identifies 1965; this is not a VIN/date authentication of the photographed survivor. Broad production dates and counts are omitted. No unprinted power, 5S tune, Gordini Jet 6 or racing specification is imported. The universal “world’s first” claim is conservatively expressed as an early production pioneer.
cars.summary: The Djet was an early production mid-engine sports-car pioneer, originating with René Bonnet before Matra took over its manufacture. The Djet 5 continued this compact Renault-powered berlinetta and helped establish Matra Sports as a road-car maker. Its importance lies in its pioneering layout rather than outright engine power.

cars.generation: Original Beta Montecarlo / Montecarlo mid-engine road family
cars.specification_market: Factory Heritage French account covers first-series Beta Montecarlo and second-series Montecarlo. Selected 1980 European Targa/Spider, with revised grille, glazed rear buttresses and electronic ignition. Original 2-litre/twin-cam/five-speed architecture is retained; no exact displacement, rating-standard conversion or torque is invented. US Scorpion’s smaller engine, SE 030 prototype and Group 5/037 competition specifications are excluded. Source production-count arithmetic is inconsistent and is not imported.
cars.summary: The Montecarlo combined Pininfarina’s purpose-designed two-seat body with a transverse mid-mounted Lampredi twin-cam engine. Its architecture and styling formed a foundation for Lancia’s Group 5 Montecarlo and Rally 037 competition projects, giving the road coupe an enduring place in Lancia’s sporting history.

cars.generation: HC-derived Firenza HP Droopsnoot performance coupe
cars.variant: HP Droopsnoot — manufacturer heritage road reference
cars.specification_market: Vauxhall’s 8 April 2020 heritage chapter identifies HP creation in 1973, five-speed first, 2279-cc slant-four and native 120-mph/7.6-second 0–60-mph claims. The claimed extra 21 bhp is not turned into an invented absolute output. Dealer Team Vauxhall context supports significance; Baby Bertha’s racing equipment/results are not assigned to the HP road car. Ordinary flat-nose Firenza/Magnum FIA paperwork is not used as an HP technical source.
cars.summary: The Firenza HP Droopsnoot paired distinctive aerodynamic front bodywork with a specially developed slant-four engine and Vauxhall’s first five-speed gearbox. It became a road-going flagship for the marque’s 1970s performance ambitions and Dealer Team Vauxhall era, earning its place beyond the ordinary Firenza and Magnum range.

cars.generation: Kadett C GT/E rear-drive sporting coupe family
cars.variant: GT/E 1.9 — February 1976 base four-speed road reference
cars.specification_market: Original Adam Opel/ONS FIA 5624 Group 1 base, valid 1 February 1976 as handwritten on PDF1, not the web index’s 2 February date. First eighteen of 53 pages rendered; cover, base engine PDF4 and gearbox PDF5 read individually. Selected 1897-cc base with Opel four-speed; Group 2 ZF five-speed/ratios, later 1979-cc engine, extensions and race tune are excluded. Manufacturer retrospective supplies Bosch injection and native 77 kW/105 PS without relabelling 225-PS competition engines as road output.
cars.summary: The Kadett C GT/E revived Opel’s Rallye-Kadett tradition with Bosch fuel injection and a distinctive yellow-and-black road coupe. Its development into the works rally cars driven by Walter Röhrl and Rauno Aaltonen makes this rear-drive GT/E an important European sporting icon, rather than an admission of the ordinary Kadett range.
